questions.questionText:
A student determines the diameter of a metal ball.
Which apparatus is needed to get an accurate measurement?

options.text: a ruler and a protractor
a ruler only
a protractor and a set square
a ruler and two rectangular blocks

questions.questionText:
A piece of paper torn out of an exercise book is shown.
What is being described?

options.text: gravitational charge
gravitational field
gravitational mass
gravitational potential energy

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows one liquid floating on top of another liquid.
liquid P
liquid Q
Which statement explains why liquid P floats on top of liquid Q?

options.text: The mass of liquid Q is greater than the mass of liquid P.
The mass of 1cm3 of liquid Q is greater than the mass of 1cm3 of liquid P.
The volume of liquid Q is greater than the volume of liquid P.
The volume of 1g of liquid Q is greater than the volume of 1g of liquid P.

questions.questionText:
A spring has a spring constant k.
What is a possible unit for k?

options.text: metre per newton
newton metre
newton per metre
newton per metre squared

questions.questionText: Which statement about the moment of a force is not correct?

options.text: If an object is balanced about a pivot, the resultant moment on the object must be zero.
The moment of a force is a measure of its turning effect.
The moment of a force about a point is equal to: force  perpendicular distance from the point.
The moment of a force about a point increases when the perpendicular distance of the force from the point decreases.

questions.questionText:
A machine is very efficient.
What does this mean?

options.text: It produces a large amount of power.
It uses very little energy.
It wastes very little energy.
It works very quickly.

questions.questionText:
Brownian motion is the random movement of microscopic particles in a liquid or gas.
Which statement about Brownian motion is correct?

options.text: Brownian motion only occurs when the liquid or gas is heated.
Much heavier fast-moving particles that cannot be seen collide with the microscopic particles.
Much lighter fast-moving particles that cannot be seen collide with the microscopic particles.
The microscopic particles move to avoid the fast-moving liquid or gas molecules.

questions.questionText:
The distance between two electricity pylons is 60m. The cable that connects the two pylons is
62m in length.
Why is the cable longer than the distance between the two pylons?

options.text: to allow for contraction of the cable in cold weather
to create a slope in the cable for electrons to flow down
to keep the current low and the voltage high
to reduce magnetic fields around the cable

questions.questionText:
A glass beaker contains a mass of 0.20kg of water at a temperature of 20°C.
The specific heat capacity of water is 4200J/(kg°C).
Which statement about convection is not correct?

options.text: It enables water in a pan on a cooker to get evenly heated.
It happens in liquids and gases.
It occurs because cooler liquids rise above warmer liquids.
It occurs because the density of a liquid decreases when it is heated.

questions.questionText:
Iron is a better conductor of thermal energy than rubber.
Which statement explains this?

options.text: Electrons in iron can move from one part of the iron to another. Electrons in rubber cannot move in this way.
Electrons in iron vibrate with more energy than those in rubber.
Positive particles in iron can move from one part of the iron to another. Positive particles in rubber cannot move in this way.
Positive particles in iron vibrate with more energy than those in rubber.

questions.questionText:
Two metal cans are identical, except that one has a shiny silver outer surface and the other has a
dull black outer surface. They each have the same mass of hot water at the same temperature
sealed inside them. They are both in a vacuum in the darkness of outer space.
How does the temperature of the water in each one change?

options.text: The temperature of the water does not change.
The water in the black can cools more slowly than that in the silver can.
The water in the silver can cools more slowly than that in the black can.
They both cool down at the same rate.

questions.questionText:
A ray of light reflects from a plane mirror.
The angle between the incident ray and the surface of the mirror is 35°.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The angle of incidence is 35°.
The angle of incidence is 55°.
The angle of reflection is 70°.
The angle of reflection is 110°.

All rays initially parallel to the principal axis of the lens are refracted through the principal focus.
The focal length of the lens is the distance between the image and the principal focus.

questions.questionText:
Ultraviolet radiation and infrared radiation are both parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.
However, they differ in wavelength and frequency.
Which row describes how they differ?
ultraviolet infrared

options.text: longer wavelength higher frequency than infrared than ultraviolet
longer wavelength lower frequency than infrared than ultraviolet
shorter wavelength higher frequency than infrared than ultraviolet
shorter wavelength lower frequency than infrared than ultraviolet

questions.questionText:

although the loudness of the sound produced does not change, the pitch varies.
Which row describes the amplitude and the frequency of the sound?
amplitude frequency

options.text: constant constant
constant varying
varying constant
varying varying

questions.questionText:
A fully charged battery stores a charge of 18000C. The battery is charged with a current of
830mA.
How long does it take to fully charge a completely discharged battery?

options.text: about 10 minutes
about 3.5 hours
about 4 hours
about 6 hours

questions.questionText: What is the definition of electromotive force?

options.text: the electrical work done by a source in moving a unit charge around a complete circuit
the electrical work done by a unit charge passing through a component
the mechanical work done by a source in moving a unit charge around a complete circuit
the mechanical work done by a unit charge passing through a component

questions.questionText:
Lamps can be connected in series or in parallel to a power supply.
What is an advantage of connecting the lamps in parallel rather than in series?

options.text: All of the lamps can be switched on and off using the same switch.
Fewer connecting leads are needed to make the circuit.
When one lamp stops working, the others may continue to work.
Less power is transferred from the supply.

questions.questionText: The lamps on a bicycle are powered by a simple electrical generator.

options.text: The current in the lamps decreases as the speed of rotation increases.
The current in the lamps decreases when the magnet is replaced by a stronger magnet.
The output electromotive force (e.m.f.) will be higher if the gap between the magnet and the coil is bigger.
The output e.m.f. will be higher if there are more turns on the coil.

questions.questionText:
A current-carrying coil in the magnetic field between the poles of two magnets experiences a
turning effect.
Which change would decrease the turning effect?

options.text: decreasing the distance between the magnets
increasing the current in the coil
using stronger magnets
decreasing the number of turns on the coil

questions.questionText:
A beta-particle is a fast-moving electron.
Which statement explains how beta-particles are emitted from an atom?

options.text: An electron is emitted as a beta-particle from an inner electron shell of the atom.
An electron is emitted as a beta-particle from an outer electron shell of the atom.
A neutron changes into a proton and a beta-particle is emitted from the nucleus.
A proton changes into a neutron and a beta-particle is emitted from the nucleus.

options.text: less than one minute  only

questions.questionText:
Comets move round the Sun.
Which statement describes the orbit of a comet?

options.text: The orbit is circular with the Sun at the centre of the circle.
The orbit is circular with the Sun not at the centre of the circle.
The orbit is elliptical with the Sun at the centre of the ellipse.
The orbit is elliptical with the Sun not at the centre of the ellipse.
